title: Request or install approved work software
section: # Request or install approved work software
text:
# Request or install approved work software

Install work software only through the organization's approved software catalog or IT process. Approval and licensing requirements depend on the software and role.

title: Request or install approved work software
text:
## Steps

1. Search the company software catalog for the application and verify the publisher and supported version.

2. Review any eligibility, manager approval, or license requirements shown in the catalog.

3. If self-service installation is offered, start it from the catalog and follow the managed installer prompts.

4. If the application is not listed or requires approval, submit a software request with the business need and device details requested by the form.

5. Restart the application or device if the installer requests it, then confirm the application opens as expected.

title: Request or install approved work software
text:
## Security reminders

Do not download installers from unofficial websites, use a personal license for company work, or bypass administrator controls. Do not disable security tools to complete an installation.

title: Request or install approved work software
text:
## Escalate to IT

Contact the software support team if the catalog reports an installation failure, the application is missing after a successful request, or a license or compatibility error appears. Include the application name, catalog version, device type, request reference, and error text. Do not share license keys or administrator credentials.

title: Troubleshoot access to a business application
section: # Troubleshoot access to a business application
text:
# Troubleshoot access to a business application

Use these checks when a work application rejects a sign-in or reports that access is not authorized.

title: Troubleshoot access to a business application
text:
## Steps

1. Confirm you are using the organization's official application URL and the correct work account, especially if you use multiple accounts.

2. Check the error message and confirm the device date and time are correct.

3. If the application uses single sign-on, start from the approved company portal and complete MFA only for a sign-in you initiated.

4. Retry in a supported browser. If allowed by company policy, use a private window to check whether a stale browser session is involved. Do not share browser session links.

5. Confirm whether the application requires a role, group membership, license, or manager approval. Submit an access request through the approved process if needed.

title: Troubleshoot access to a business application
text:
## Security reminders

Never approve an unexpected MFA prompt or send passwords, verification codes, cookies, or session tokens to anyone. Do not try to gain access through another employee's account.

title: Troubleshoot access to a business application
text:
## Escalate to IT

Contact the application support team if access is denied after approval, the sign-in loops, or the service reports an outage. Include the official app name, error text, time, device and browser, and any request reference. Exclude passwords, MFA codes, and session tokens from screenshots or tickets.

title: Troubleshoot a corporate Wi-Fi connection
text:
# Troubleshoot a corporate Wi-Fi connection

Use these basic checks when a managed device cannot connect to the expected corporate wireless network.

title: Troubleshoot a corporate Wi-Fi connection
text:
## Steps

1. Confirm Wi-Fi is enabled and airplane mode is off.

2. Select the exact corporate network name provided by IT. Avoid similarly named or open networks.

3. Move closer to an approved access point and retry once. If other trusted devices are available, check whether they can connect.

4. If your organization provides a Wi-Fi setup guide, follow it to rejoin the network. Do not install a certificate or profile from an unverified prompt or website.

5. Restart the device if practical, then try connecting again.

6. Record the displayed message and whether the device receives a network connection.

title: Troubleshoot a corporate Wi-Fi connection
text:
## Security reminders

Do not bypass certificate warnings, share the corporate Wi-Fi password publicly, or use an unknown network to access company systems. Use the organization's approved guest network only when authorized.

title: Troubleshoot a corporate Wi-Fi connection
text:
## Escalate to IT

Contact IT if the network is missing, authentication repeatedly fails, a certificate warning appears, or several users in the same location are affected. Include the building or area, device type, network name, error text, and time observed. Never send passwords or private network keys in a ticket.

title: Troubleshoot Outlook email synchronization
text:
# Troubleshoot Outlook email synchronization

Use these checks when Outlook is not sending, receiving, or updating messages. Do not delete mailbox data or change account settings unless IT instructs you to.

title: Troubleshoot Outlook email synchronization
text:
## Steps

1. Confirm the device is online and that other approved sites or applications work.

2. Check the organization's service-status page, if available, for an email outage or scheduled maintenance.

3. In Outlook, confirm the correct work account is selected and that the application is not in an offline or disconnected mode.

4. Close and reopen Outlook once. If convenient, compare with the organization's approved webmail page to determine whether the issue is limited to the desktop app.

5. Install Outlook updates through the normal company update or software process, then restart the application.

6. Note whether the issue affects all folders or only a particular mailbox or message.

title: Troubleshoot Outlook email synchronization
text:
## Security reminders

Do not forward sensitive messages to a personal account to test delivery. Do not share passwords, MFA codes, or mail-session links with support.

title: Troubleshoot Outlook email synchronization
text:
## Escalate to IT

Contact IT if synchronization remains delayed, Outlook repeatedly requests credentials, messages are missing, or webmail and desktop results differ. Include the error text, approximate time of the last successful sync, affected device, and whether other users are affected. Do not remove an Outlook profile or local data file unless directed by IT.

title: Reset a password or resolve an account lockout
section: # Reset a password or resolve an account lockout
text:
# Reset a password or resolve an account lockout

Use only the organization's approved password-reset portal or identity support process. Exact reset and unlock rules vary by organization.

title: Reset a password or resolve an account lockout
text:
## Steps

1. Open the password-reset portal from a trusted company link or bookmark. Do not follow reset links from unexpected email or chat messages.

2. Complete the portal's identity verification using your enrolled multifactor authentication method.

3. Choose a new password that meets the organization's displayed requirements. Do not reuse a password from another service.

4. If the account is locked, follow the portal's unlock option or wait for the stated lockout period before trying again. Repeated guesses can extend a lockout.

5. After a successful reset, sign in to the required work applications and update the password only in approved device prompts.

title: Reset a password or resolve an account lockout
text:
## Security reminders

IT will not need your password or one-time verification code. Never send either by email or chat. Do not use unofficial reset tools or attempt to bypass identity verification.

title: Reset a password or resolve an account lockout
text:
## Escalate to IT

Contact the identity support team if the portal cannot verify you, no enrolled MFA method is available, the account remains locked after the portal's instructions, or you suspect someone else changed your password. Share the error and approximate time, but not the password or verification code.

title: Basic checks for a slow work laptop
section: # Basic checks for a slow work laptop
text:
# Basic checks for a slow work laptop

These low-risk checks can help identify common causes of poor performance on a managed work device.

title: Basic checks for a slow work laptop
text:
## Steps

1. Save your work and restart the laptop if it has been running for a long time.

2. Close applications and browser tabs you recognize but are not using. Do not terminate unfamiliar security or management processes.

3. Check the operating system's built-in task monitor for an application using unusually high CPU or memory. Note the application name; do not disable endpoint protection.

4. Check available storage in system settings. Use only organization-approved cleanup tools, and do not delete work files to free space.

5. Install pending updates through the normal company update process and restart when prompted.

6. Make sure vents are not blocked. If the device is unusually hot, noisy, or shuts down, stop intensive work and contact IT.

title: Basic checks for a slow work laptop
text:
## Security reminders

Do not install third-party cleanup or driver tools, change security settings, or remove managed software to improve speed.

title: Basic checks for a slow work laptop
text:
## Escalate to IT

Contact IT if slowness persists after a restart, affects several managed applications, or is accompanied by overheating, disk errors, crashes, or unusual security alerts. Include when the issue began, affected applications, recent changes, and any error messages. Do not attach confidential files unless requested through an approved support channel.

title: Troubleshoot a corporate VPN connection
text:
# Troubleshoot a corporate VPN connection

Use these checks when the approved corporate VPN client will not connect. Follow your organization's VPN and security policies; these general steps do not replace them.

title: Troubleshoot a corporate VPN connection
text:
## Steps

1. Confirm the device has an internet connection before starting the VPN. If possible, test a normal approved website.

2. Confirm the device date and time are correct. Authentication can fail when the clock is substantially out of sync.

3. Open the approved VPN client and sign in with the corporate account. Complete the expected multifactor authentication prompt only when you initiated the sign-in.

4. Read the exact client error and note when it occurred. Close and reopen the client once, then retry.

5. Check for client updates through the organization's software catalog or IT instructions. Do not download a VPN client from an unofficial site.

6. If permitted, restart the device and try again on a trusted network.

title: Troubleshoot a corporate VPN connection
text:
## Security reminders

Never share your password or one-time codes with support staff. Do not disable endpoint protection, bypass certificate warnings, or approve an unexpected MFA request to make the connection work.

title: Troubleshoot a corporate VPN connection
text:
## Escalate to IT

Contact IT if the issue continues, affects multiple users, follows a password or MFA change, or displays a certificate, account-lock, or policy error. Include the error text, time, device operating system, VPN client version, and network type. Do not include passwords, recovery codes, or session tokens.
